headline: Google gets hammered -5.1% last night as top AI researchers defect to rivals, while Pilbara Minerals tanked -6% today on no fresh news — a rough day for the portfolio.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS closed down nearly 6% today in a rough session for lithium stocks. There was no specific fresh catalyst — this looks like broader market weakness and continued pessimism around lithium prices. The stock is now down almost 18% on your total investment.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG dropped 5.1% last night after news broke that multiple high-profile AI researchers — including people from its DeepMind and Gemini teams — have defected to rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. Markets are worried Google is losing its edge in the AI race at exactly the wrong time, given how much it's spending on AI infrastructure.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT fell 3.1% last night, dragged down partly by the broader tech sell-off that hit Google hard. The NASDAQ dropped 1.4% overall, and sentiment around big-tech AI spending came under pressure. No specific Microsoft bad news — it was caught in the same wave.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid session today, up 1.47% — the best performer in the portfolio on the ASX today. Emerging markets got a lift, possibly helped by a slightly weaker US dollar and improving risk appetite in Asian markets.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI bounced 1.2% today on the ASX, which is a bit ironic given the Google AI talent exodus news. The ASX-listed ETF often moves on a lag to US tech, so today's gain likely reflects last week's positive US AI sentiment rather than today's Google headlines.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL edged up 0.62% today despite oil (WTI crude) dropping over 3% last night to US$74.26/barrel. The ASX ETF held up relatively well — it may have been buoyed by energy sector positioning, though the oil price slide is a headwind worth watching this week.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.38% today — a steady, unremarkable session. As a diversified fund holding global and Australian shares, bonds, and property, it absorbed the US tech weakness reasonably well thanks to its spread across many asset classes.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.29% today on the ASX. This ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket and tends to move on a lag — today's modest gain likely reflects last week's US market levels before last night's tech sell-off hit. Expect some pressure here in tomorrow's session.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was virtually flat last night, up just 0.2%. The GTA 6 hype continues to simmer in the background — price leak rumours and pre-sale announcement news are generating buzz — but the stock is biding its time ahead of actual release catalysts.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Talent exodus is a real problem — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Google lost multiple top DeepMind and Gemini AI researchers to OpenAI and Anthropic in the past 48 hours, and the stock fell 5.1% last night to US$348.73. This isn't just a one-day wobble — if Google's best AI people keep walking out the door, it puts their competitive position at risk right when AI is everything. Your position is still 13.4% up overall, but watch closely. No need to panic-sell, but don't add more right now.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Pilbara Minerals sliding hard — down 6% today
watch_today.detail: Pilbara closed at $5.53 today, down 5.95% with no obvious fresh catalyst. The stock is now 18% below your cost base. There is some longer-term optimism — Fastmarkets is calling a new phase where lithium demand outpaces supply — but that's a future story. Right now, sentiment is weak and there's no floor in sight. Hold unless you're prepared to average down with eyes open.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Caught in the tech sell-off — still a solid hold
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 3.1% last night to US$367.48, pulled down by the broader NASDAQ sell-off rather than any company-specific bad news. Analysts still like the Microsoft story — its AI integration into Office and Azure is steady and less dependent on retaining individual star researchers. Down 17% on your total investment, but the fundamentals haven't changed overnight.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX: US tech sell-off may flow through tomorrow
watch_today.detail: VTS gained 0.29% today on the ASX, but that's before last night's NASDAQ drop of 1.38% and S&P 500 fall of 0.41% has had a chance to be priced in. Expect VTS to face some headwind in tomorrow's session. Nothing to act on, just be aware the gain today may reverse.

watch_today.title: Oil down 3% — watch FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil fell from US$76.60 to US$74.26 last night — a drop of over 3%. FUEL.AX held up today (+0.62%), but if oil keeps sliding it will pressure the energy ETF. OPEC's latest outlook is flagging some demand concerns. No need to sell, but keep an eye on the oil price this week.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF up today — but Google headlines are a wildcard
watch_today.detail: Your AI-focused ETF bounced 1.21% today to $18.38, still slightly below your $297 cost base overall. The Google talent news is a reminder that AI leadership can shift quickly between companies. GXAI holds a basket of AI stocks so it's diversified, but GOOG is likely a meaningful weight. Worth keeping an eye on how US AI stocks open tonight.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was rough for tech — the NASDAQ fell 1.38% and the S&P 500 dropped 0.41%, driven largely by the Google AI talent exodus story hitting sentiment across big tech. Oil slid over 3% to US$74.26 a barrel, gold eased slightly to US$4,204, and the Aussie dollar barely moved at US$0.70. The ASX 200's closing data wasn't available today, but the local market held up reasonably well based on individual stock moves.

politics.summary: Light day for Australian politics in the news — a couple of stories broke but nothing with major market-moving implications today.

stories.title: US Rate Hike: What It Means for Australian Investors in 2026
stories.why_it_matters: The US Federal Reserve (America's central bank) has been hiking interest rates, and that has ripple effects for Australian investors. When US rates rise, the US dollar tends to strengthen, which can pressure the Aussie dollar lower and make your US-denominated holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) worth less when converted back to AUD. It also tends to make growth stocks look less attractive. No article text was available, so further detail is limited — but this is a macro theme worth staying across.

stories.title: Law Delay Bad News for Journalism
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian reports that a delay in media law reform is bad news for the journalism industry. No article text was available to get the specifics, but the broader story is about the ongoing fight over how tech platforms like Google and Meta pay Australian news outlets for content. Delays in this legislation leave news publishers in limbo — worth noting if you hold GOOG, as any future Australian news bargaining code changes could affect its operating costs locally.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story today — and the reason your GOOG position took a beating — is a wave of top Google AI talent walking out the door to join rivals Anthropic and OpenAI. It's the talk of the tech world right now, and it's raised real questions about whether Google can maintain its AI leadership.

stories.title: Top Google DeepMind and Gemini Researchers Defect to OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple senior AI researchers from Google's DeepMind lab and its Gemini AI team have left for rival firms Anthropic and OpenAI in the past 48 hours — a significant brain drain at exactly the moment when AI is the most important battleground in tech. One of the departing researchers is a Nobel laureate-level figure, according to reports. Markets reacted immediately, sending Google's stock down 5.1% last night. The concern is that Google's AI products could suffer if its best builders keep walking out the door, especially while the company is already spending billions on AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Nobel Laureate Moves to Anthropic — Is Internal Faith at Google Collapsing?
stories.why_it_matters: A Nobel laureate-calibre researcher joining Anthropic is a big symbolic blow for Google — these aren't junior engineers, these are the people who define where AI research goes next. When top scientists leave, they don't just take their brains — they take credibility, future papers, and often younger talent follows them. Two major departures in 48 hours has sparked questions about whether confidence inside Google's AI division is fracturing. No article text was available for more specifics.

stories.title: AI-Based Law Firm Wins in Court
stories.why_it_matters: An AI-powered law firm has won a case in court, marking a meaningful real-world milestone for AI in professional services. No article text was available for specifics on which firm or jurisdiction, but this is the kind of proof-of-concept moment that pushes AI adoption further into industries like law, accounting, and consulting. For investors in AI-focused ETFs like GXAI.AX, this is the sort of story that underpins the long-term thesis.

stories.title: The Anthropic Case Tests the Limits of AI Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: As Anthropic grows in influence — now attracting top talent from Google — regulators are starting to pay more attention to whether existing AI rules actually cover the most powerful AI labs. This article explores where current AI regulation falls short and what might need to change. For investors, it's a reminder that regulation risk is real for the whole AI sector — tighter rules could slow growth or increase costs for companies in your GXAI.AX ETF.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 wrapped up over the weekend with the Roosters picking up a win, and attention is already turning to Round 17 which kicks off Thursday. There's also some noteworthy tennis and AFL news today.

stories.title: Roosters Win Fiery Battle — Teddy Cops Brutal Knock
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters won a fiery Round 16 clash over the weekend, but skipper James Teddy took a brutal head knock in the process. His availability for Round 17 will be the big question this week. With the Broncos hosting the Roosters on Friday night at Suncorp Stadium, any Teddy injury update will be crucial for punters and fantasy leagues alike.

stories.title: 2026 NRL Signings Tracker: Hunt to Play On With Broncos; To'a Joins Sea Eagles
stories.why_it_matters: Key signings news: Broncos halfback Adam Hunt has committed to stay in Brisbane, which is great news for Broncos fans heading into Friday's home clash with the Roosters. Meanwhile Christian To'a — the powerful Sea Eagles winger — has officially joined Manly, bolstering their outside backs. Round 17 features Sea Eagles vs Storm on Saturday night, which should be a cracker.

stories.title: Serena Williams Earns Wimbledon Singles Wild Card
stories.why_it_matters: Serena Williams has been handed a Wimbledon singles wild card, continuing her remarkable comeback to professional tennis. Wimbledon starts in early July, so this is imminent. Serena hasn't played at a Grand Slam in years, and a wild card entry — rather than qualifying — means the All England Club is banking on the box office appeal. One of the biggest storylines heading into the grass-court season.

stories.title: AFL: Injury-Hit Saints Are a Worry; Blues Are Back?!
stories.why_it_matters: ESPN's AFL power rankings flag St Kilda as a major injury concern — the Saints are losing key players at a worrying rate and their season could be on the slide. On the flip side, Carlton (the Blues) are showing signs of life and may have turned a corner after a shaky start. No article text was available for exact player names and injury details, but it's the dominant AFL talking point heading into this weekend's fixtures.
